key_insight: GINNGER learns thermodynamically admissible constitutive laws by discovering the underlying GENERIC generators, rather than fitting a black-box stress operator.
engineering_relevance: This offers a physics-preserving way to build rheology models that generalize across shear, extensional, and mixed flows while maintaining objectivity and the first and second laws of thermodynamics.
method: Embed the GENERIC formalism into neural constitutive discovery to enforce thermodynamic consistency by construction.
Learn thermodynamic generators in the eigenspace of the polymer conformation tensor, giving a kinematics-independent state representation.
Use flow kinematics only as an external driver, enabling one model to span multiple deformation protocols and geometries.
evidence_signal: The approach is validated on high-fidelity simulations, where it reconstructs constitutive behavior accurately and predicts flow fields in previously unseen geometries.
watch_item: The spectral state-space formulation may depend on robust eigen-decomposition and high-quality microstructural data, which could be challenging in noisy experimental settings.
paper_title: A GENERIC-Informed Neural Network for Generative Rheology
